unit.unitTitle: Numbers to 100, and How Things Are
unit.unitOverview: Count to a hundred, and read prices and dates. Talk about people and things: tall, kind, cheap. Say how you do it: quickly, carefully. Add too: me too.

Speaking: tap the mic. Say it. Listen back.

Practice: write. Check with the answers.

visual.lectureScript:
Hello! This is Unit 9.
In this unit, you count to a hundred.
You read prices and dates.
You talk about people and things.
First, count in tens. Listen and repeat.
Ten, twenty, thirty, forty, fifty.
Sixty, seventy, eighty, ninety, a hundred.
Now listen to the end of the word.
Thir-TEEN is thirteen. It is long at the end.
THIR-ty is thirty. It is short at the end.
Say them: thirteen, thirty. Fifteen, fifty.
Four has a u. Forty has no u.
Now the ten and the one together.
Twenty-one. Thirty-five. Sixty-eight. Ninety-nine.
Say the ten first, then the one.
Now prices. A price is a number.
What is the price? The price is 45.
The pen is 2. It is cheap.
The phone is 95. It is expensive.
You pay at the desk.
Now dates. Listen and repeat.
The eleventh. The twelfth. The twentieth. The thirtieth.
Now listen: twenty-first, twenty-second, twenty-third.
They end like first, second and third.
The market is on Saturday the 21st.
Now people. He is tall. She is young.
My neighbour is kind and friendly.
Two words? Put and between them.
Two people? The word is the same. They are kind.
These words are for things too: a busy street, a strong bag.
Now how you do a thing.
He walks. How? Quickly.
Add the letters l and y: quick, quickly.
Careful, carefully. Loud, loudly. Clear, clearly.
Easy is different: easily.
The word goes after the thing you do.
She drives carefully. Please speak clearly.
Now a small word: too.
I like tea. My friend likes tea too.
Or say it short: Me too.
Too goes at the end.
Last: my, his, her and its, with a describing word.
My old bag. Her new phone.
For a thing, say its.
The shop is small. Its door is red.
The watch is new. Its price is 60.
Now go to Words. Goodbye!

readings.setting: A busy street with a shop and a café.
readings.passageScript:
My street is busy in the morning.
The shopkeeper is Tomas. He is tall and strong.
He carries the boxes quickly and easily.
His shop is small. Its door is green.
Next to it is a café. Nadia works there.
She is young and friendly. She speaks clearly.
My neighbour Lena is seventy-two. She is kind.
She walks slowly and carefully.
I like my street. My sister likes it too.

readings.title: Prices and Dates: Read Them Carefully
readings.setting: Numbers you meet at a shop, a market or an office.
readings.passageScript:
Prices and dates are numbers. Read them carefully.
A price: 45. Say forty-five.
A date: the 21st. Say the twenty-first.
Most dates end like fourteenth: the 14th, the 20th, the 30th.
The 21st, 22nd and 23rd end like first, second and third.
The 11th, 12th and 13th end like fourteenth.
Thirteen and thirty sound the same when you speak quickly.
Say the end clearly: thir-TEEN, THIR-ty.
You do not hear the number? Say: Sorry? Please repeat.

grammar.title: Twenty-one to a hundred
grammar.explanation:
Count in tens: twenty, thirty, forty.
For 21 to 99, say the ten, then the one.
Write a dash between them: forty-five.
100 is a hundred, or one hundred.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
20 twenty      60 sixty
30 thirty      70 seventy
40 forty       80 eighty
50 fifty       90 ninety
100 a hundred

21 twenty-one
35 thirty-five
47 forty-seven
99 ninety-nine

13 thir-TEEN: long at the end
30 THIR-ty: short at the end

four, fourteen — forty (no u)
grammar.workedExample:
Write 68 as words.
1. 68 is 60 and 8.
2. 60 is sixty.
3. 8 is eight.
4. Put a dash between them: sixty-eight.
5. Check the list: 60 sixty. Yes.
grammar.commonMistake:
Four has a u. Forty does not.
No: fourty.
Yes: forty.
It is easy to say 30 like 13.
Say THIR-ty, short at the end.
Thir-TEEN is long at the end.
grammar.memoryTip: Forty: no u. The ten first, then the one.
grammar.answerKey:
1. twenty-four  2. forty  3. fifty-one  4. sixteen  5. sixty  6. seventy-three  7. eighty-eight  8. a hundred (or one hundred)
Wrong on 2? Forty has no u.
Wrong on 4 or 5? 16 is sixteen. 60 is sixty. Look at the end: teen or ty.

grammar.title: Eleventh to fiftieth: dates
grammar.explanation:
A date says which day it is: the 14th.
Most dates end like fourteenth.
The 21st, 22nd and 23rd end like first, second and third.
The 11th, 12th and 13th end like fourteenth.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
11th  eleventh
12th  twelfth
13th  thirteenth
14th  fourteenth
20th  twentieth
21st  twenty-first
22nd  twenty-second
23rd  twenty-third
24th  twenty-fourth
30th  thirtieth
31st  thirty-first
40th  fortieth
50th  fiftieth

twenty — twentieth
thirty — thirtieth

Say the before a date: on the 21st.
On Saturday the 21st.
grammar.workedExample:
Write 22 as a date.
1. 22 is twenty and two.
2. Two as a date is second.
3. So 22 is twenty-second.
4. As a number: 22nd.
5. Say it: the twenty-second.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to put th on every date.
No: the 21th, the 22th.
Yes: the 21st, the 22nd.
Look at the last number: 1 is st, 2 is nd, 3 is rd.
11, 12 and 13 are different: the 11th, the 12th, the 13th.
grammar.memoryTip: Look at the last number: 1st, 2nd, 3rd. The rest: th.

grammar.title: Quick, quickly: say how you do it
grammar.explanation:
These words say how you do a thing.
Many end in the letters l and y: quickly, loudly.
The word goes after the thing you do.
He walks quickly.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
quick — quickly
loud — loudly
clear — clearly
careful — carefully
slow — slowly
easy — easily  (y changes to i)

He walks quickly.
She drives carefully.
They talk loudly.
Please speak clearly.
I can read it easily.

He walks. How? Quickly.
grammar.workedExample:
She speaks. How? The word is clear.
1. Start with clear.
2. Add ly: clearly.
3. Put it after speaks.
4. She speaks clearly.
5. Check: speaks, then clearly. Yes.
grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to leave out ly.
No: She drives careful.
Yes: She drives carefully.
Easy is different.
No: easyly.
Yes: easily.
grammar.memoryTip: How do you do it? Add ly: quickly.
grammar.practice:
Write the word with ly.
1. He walks ___. (quick)
2. Please speak ___. (clear)
3. She carries the glass ___. (careful)
4. They sing ___. (loud)
5. I can count to 50 ___. (easy)
6. The bus goes ___. (slow)
7. Write your address ___. (careful)
grammar.answerKey:
1. quickly  2. clearly  3. carefully  4. loudly  5. easily  6. slowly  7. carefully
Wrong on 5? Easy: the y changes to i. Easily.
Wrong on 3 or 7? Careful has one l. Carefully has two.

grammar.title: Too at the end: me too
grammar.explanation:
Too says: the same.
Put too at the end.
Me too is a short answer. It means: the same for me.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
A: I like tea.
B: I like tea too.
B: Me too.

Omar is tall. His brother is tall too.
The bag is cheap. It is strong too.
I can swim. I can cook too.

too — the same, at the end
two — the number 2
to — go to the shop
grammar.workedExample:
Ana is busy. Ben is busy.
Say it with too.
1. Ben is the same as Ana.
2. Say the line for Ben: Ben is busy.
3. Add too at the end.
4. Ana is busy. Ben is busy too.
grammar.commonMistake:
Too, two and to sound the same.
No: I like it to.
No: I like it two.
Yes: I like it too.
Too has two of the letter o.
grammar.memoryTip: The same? Add too at the end.
grammar.practice:
Write the second line with too.
1. I am busy. My brother is busy ___.
2. Omar is kind. Hana is kind ___.
3. A: I like music. B: Me ___.
4. The bag is cheap. It is strong ___.
5. Write it with too: Mia can swim. Leo can swim.
6. Two or too? I have got ___ pens.
7. Two or too? She is tall. He is tall ___.
grammar.answerKey:
1. too  2. too  3. too  4. too  5. Mia can swim. Leo can swim too.  6. two  7. too
Wrong on 6? Two pens: the number 2.

grammar.title: Tall and kind: describing words after is
grammar.explanation:
Describing words: tall, young, kind, busy.
Put them after is or are: She is tall.
Two words? Put and between them: tall and kind.
Use them for people and for things.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
He is tall.
She is young and friendly.
They are kind.
The shop is busy.
The bag is strong and cheap.

a tall man — the man is tall
a busy street — the street is busy

One person or two, the same word:
He is kind. They are kind.
grammar.workedExample:
Describe Omar. He is 25. He helps people.
1. 25 is not old: young.
2. He helps people: kind.
3. Two words? Put and between them.
4. Omar is young and kind.
grammar.commonMistake:
Describing words have no s.
No: They are talls.
Yes: They are tall.
No: two beautifuls gardens.
Yes: two beautiful gardens.
grammar.memoryTip: Two people, one word: they are kind. No s.
grammar.practice:

7. The women are beautifuls.
grammar.answerKey:
1. My father is tall.  2. The nurses are kind.  3. The street is busy.  4. She is young and friendly.  5. The bag is strong and cheap.  6. They are busy.  7. The women are beautiful.
Wrong on 2 or 6? Two or more: are. No s on kind or busy.
Number 7: no s on beautiful.

grammar.title: Her new phone, its price
grammar.explanation:
First say who has it: my, his, her.
Then a describing word, then the thing: her new phone.
For a thing, say its: The shop is busy. Its door is red.
grammar.ruleAndExamples:
my — My bag is old. My old bag.
your — Your phone is new. Your new phone.
his — His brother is tall.
her — Her friend is kind.
its — The pen is cheap. Its price is 1.
our — Our room is small.
their — Their garden is beautiful.

who has it + describing word + thing:
her new phone
its red door
grammar.workedExample:
The bag is new. The colour of the bag is black.
Say it with its.
1. The bag is a thing.
2. A thing: its.
3. The colour of the bag: its colour.

grammar.commonMistake:
It is easy to use his or her for a thing.
No: The shop is busy. His door is red.
Yes: The shop is busy. Its door is red.
A man: his. A woman: her. A thing: its.
grammar.memoryTip: A thing has its: its price, its colour.

1. His  2. Her  3. Its  4. My  5. Their  6. Its  7. His
Wrong on 3 or 6? The shop and the watch are things. A thing: its.
Its has no ' in it: its price, not it's price.

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: forty — 40 is forty, with no u. Fourty is a spelling mistake. Fourteen is 14. Four is 4.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: seventy-three — 73 is 70 and 3: seventy-three. Thirty-seven is 37, so the numbers swap. Seventeen is 17, not 70. Thirteen is 13, not 3.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: fifteen — 15 is fifteen, with a long end. Fifty is 50, so look at the end: teen or ty. Five is 5. Fiveteen is not a word.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: the 21st — 21 ends in 1, like first: the 21st. Th is for dates like the 24th. Nd goes with 2: the 22nd. Rd goes with 3: the 23rd.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: twelfth — 12th is twelfth: the v changes to f. Twelveth keeps the v. Twentieth is 20th. Twelve is 12, not a date.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: carefully — Drives is what she does. How? Carefully. Careful has no ly. Carefuly has one l, and carefully has two. Quick has no ly. And quick is not careful.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: easily — Easy ends in y. The y changes to i: easily. Easyly keeps the y. Easly has no i. Easy has no ly.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: too — Too means the same for me. Two is the number 2. To goes before a place: go to the shop. For goes before a person: for my sister.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Hana is kind too. — Too goes at the end: Hana is kind too. Hana too kind has no is. Two is the number 2. Too does not go first.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: tall — Two people, the same word: tall. Describing words have no s. A tall needs a thing after it, like a tall man. Tall is has is in the wrong place.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: Its — The shop is a thing. A thing: its. His is for a man. Her is for a woman. It is the shop, not who has the door.
answerKey.reviewStatus: Reviewed: script review and curriculum sign-off, 2026-08-01

answerKey.answerOrGuidance: The watch is expensive. — 95 is a big price, so the watch is expensive. 5 is a small price, so the bag is cheap. The watch is not cheap. Money is what you pay with.
